topic: What if your strength doubled every day?

script.text: Monday, six a.m., your alarm goes off. You slap it. The alarm clock is now in two pieces. That's day one.

Here's how it works. Say today you can lift fifty kilos. About one heavy suitcase. Tomorrow at six, a hundred. The day after, two hundred. Then four hundred. Eight hundred. Doesn't sound so crazy, right?

That's the trick with doubling. It starts slow, and then it explodes. On day ten, you can lift fifty-one tonnes. More than a fully loaded truck. On day twenty, over fifty-two thousand tonnes. That's about the weight of the Titanic. That's real. Fifty kilos, doubled twenty times.
Now the rules. Only your strength doubles. Not your speed. Not your size. You look exactly the same as you did last week.
And your bones, your skin, your tendons? Completely normal. Fourteen-year-old normal. Remember that. It matters later.
This is what if your strength doubled every day.

science.claim: Fifty kilos doubled ten times is about fifty-one tonnes, more than a fully loaded truck.
science.working: 50 kg x 2^10 = 51,200 kg. The EU limit for an articulated lorry is 40 t (44 t for intermodal transport).
science.source: Arithmetic; EU Council Directive 96/53/EC (weights and dimensions of road vehicles)

science.claim: Fifty kilos doubled twenty times is about the weight of the Titanic.
science.working: 50 kg x 2^20 = 52,428,800 kg = 52,429 t. Titanic's displacement was 52,310 long tons (about 53,150 t).
science.source: Arithmetic; Encyclopedia Titanica / Titanic's specifications (displacement 52,310 tons)
